scenes.title: Open-source product demos
scenes.talkingPoints: Lead with the product category, ownership model, and zero-backend boundary.

actions.title: Free and open source
actions.text: Apache 2.0 and self-hosted: no account, backend, or hosted workspace.
actions.narration: ScreenReel is a free, open-source demo recorder. Apache 2.0, no account, no backend, and nothing hosted for you to trust.

actions.title: Open-source product demos
actions.text: Record once, keep the flow in your repo, and play it inside your product.
actions.narration: Record a walkthrough once, keep it as a file in your repository, and play it inside your own product. Let's build one.

actions.note: Move to a new scene before navigation

scenes.title: Record by using the app
scenes.talkingPoints: Capture typing, selects, toggles, sliders, clicks, and navigation as editable actions.

actions.title: Record by using the app
actions.text: Typing, selects, toggles, and sliders you perform become editable actions.
actions.narration: This is the Demo Lab, a small test app. The tour names the demo, picks an audience, turns on presenter notes, and sets the pace. Each one is a real browser event, and Studio saves each one as an action you can edit.

actions.note: Keep presenter notes beside the flow

scenes.title: Emphasise the real interface
scenes.talkingPoints: Reorder a scene, then capture highlight and spotlight actions on stable real targets.

actions.title: Emphasise the real interface
actions.text: Point at a real element to capture a highlight or a spotlight.
actions.narration: Drag a scene to change the order. To show something without clicking it, point at the real element, and it becomes a highlight in the flow. Then generate the outputs.

actions.note: Move to a new scene before navigation

scenes.title: One flow, three outputs
scenes.talkingPoints: Show live playback, self-playing link, rendered video, and the repository source together.

actions.title: One flow, three outputs
actions.text: Live inside the product, a self-playing link, or a rendered video.
actions.narration: One flow, three outputs. It plays live inside your product, opens as a self-playing link, and renders to video.

actions.title: A readable flow
actions.text: The same JSON lives in your repository, next to the code it demos.
actions.narration: All three come from the same JSON file, which you review and version next to your code.

scenes.title: Repair before customers see a break
scenes.talkingPoints: Validation catches missing targets and Flow Doctor repairs fingerprinted selectors.

actions.note: Maintenance is part of the workflow

actions.title: Repair before it breaks
actions.text: Validation catches broken targets; flow doctor repairs them.
actions.narration: When your product changes, flow doctor checks every target and repairs the selectors that moved, before a customer sees a broken demo.

actions.note: Return to the landing page for the close

scenes.title: Watch it, inspect it, own it
scenes.talkingPoints: Close on the two highest-intent actions: the live demo and the repository.

actions.title: Watch it, inspect it, own it
actions.text: Run the live demo, or read every line on GitHub.
actions.narration: That was ScreenReel, playing itself. Read every line on GitHub, and put it in your own product.

scenes.title: Emphasise the product story
scenes.talkingPoints: Show a single target, a sequence, a spotlight, an anchored callout, and the code behind a step.

scenes.title: Interact with real controls
scenes.talkingPoints: The same executor can click, hover, focus, type, set, toggle, and move sliders.

scenes.title: Continue across routes
scenes.talkingPoints: Navigation retains active flow and scene position in project-scoped session storage.

scenes.title: Drag, pointer, and delayed state
scenes.talkingPoints: The remaining actions run against the fixtures on this second route: a drag board, a raw pointer target, delayed state, and a safe page function.
